title: GreenWave pilot - canary traffic orchestra and rollback playbook
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on canary traffic orchestration, refining signal thresholds, and validating rollback/runbook steps. Agreed to a dry-run of the traffic shift on staging next Wednesday; Redwood to provide canary metric dashboard and updated runbook. Security questions around KMS and audit logs still pending; SecOps to review next week.
topics: Traffic shift orchestration (A/B vs gradual ramp)
action_items: Marcus Ortiz: run 2x latency/99p benchmarks with KV-cache on quantized model by 2026-11-24
Sara Martins: prepare staging traffic generator (burst and steady) and share config by 2026-11-23
Tomas Vega: circulate KMS/SOC2 questions to Redwood security by 2026-11-25
Alicia Chen: share updated canary dashboard link and runbook draft by 2026-11-22
next_steps: Schedule dry-run traffic shift in staging (target 2026-11-25)
Redwood to deliver canary dashboard and alert playbook link
Customer SecOps to review KMS/audit docs and follow up in a security call
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CSM); Liam Howard (GreenWave Head of ML), Sara Martins (Platform Eng), Tomas Vega (SecOps), Nora Patel (SRE)

Summary: quick check-in from pilot week 5, focused on canary traffic plan, instrumentation gaps, and a dry-run schedule. Agreement on runbook edits and owners.

---
[00:00] Alicia Chen: alright everyone thanks for hopping on, we've got 50 minutes, agenda is canary orchestration, metrics gating, rollback playbook and security follow ups. quick status check from your side, Liam?
[00:22] Liam Howard: yeah thanks Alicia, overall pilot is looking good — throughput is holding, cost is in the ballpark. we did see a few 99p spikes yesterday during the prefix caching experiment, so we want to make sure the canary will catch that.
[00:40] Marcus Ortiz: when you say spikes, is that correlated with token lengths or concurrency bursts? we saw a pattern that long-context requests plus small batch sizes hit the 99p.
[00:55] Liam Howard: mostly long context, and some ad-hoc traffic from our analytics workers — they weren't using the new client header so they bypassed prefix caching, that was my fault.
[01:12] Sara Martins: for staging we can route those analytics flows into a separate lane, but we need to validate the traffic generator first.
[01:25] Alicia Chen: ok good. Marcus, are the latency benches you ran last week with KV cache reproducible in staging? i remember the numbers but want to see the same profile under the canary policy.
[01:40] Marcus Ortiz: yes, i'll re-run them with the quantized model path and kv caching toggled. quick note — the runtime picks a different kernel for 4k sequences which slightly narrows the median but leaves tail variability. we'll capture p50/p95/p99.
[01:58] Tomas Vega: just to flag from SecOps: we need the KMS flow documented for the private key rotation and we also want to see audit logs for model access — specifically per-token traceability is ideal, otherwise per-request is ok. is that possible with the private deployment?
[02:18] Priya Rao: we can pull the audit logs, Redwood Private exposes request-level audit and integrates with customer KMS/HSM, but we'll confirm the retention window and export formats.
[02:34] Nora Patel: retention window matters — 90 days minimum for our compliance.
[02:41] Alicia Chen: got it — action for Tomas and Alicia to sync offline with security docs. we'll include that as an action item.

--- Topics: Canary gating details 
[02:55] Alicia Chen: ok let's walk through the canary gating we proposed: initial 5% traffic for 30 minutes, check p99 latency + error rate + hallucination/regression signals from your eval set. then ramp to 25% for an hour if stable, then to 100% in a controlled window. open to A/B instead?
[03:18] Sara Martins: our concern is partial-session affinity — some of our frontends use sticky sessions, so A/B could bias results. gradual ramp is safer.
[03:31] Marcus Ortiz: gradual ramp with session affinity consideration — we can route NEW sessions to the canary to avoid mixing cache states. also plan to use prefix/KV warmups before opening traffic.
[03:47] Liam Howard: what about automatic rollback triggers? we want automation not manual-only.
[03:52] Marcus Ortiz: propose automated circuit breaker: if p99 > baseline + 250ms for two consecutive evaluation windows OR error rate increases > 1%, auto-shift traffic back and notify runbook on-call. baseline is rolling medians from last 24h of production traffic.
[04:13] Sara Martins: the 250ms seems reasonable but can we make it a percentage too? some models have lower baseline.
[04:20] Marcus Ortiz: yeah we can make it max(250ms, 25% of baseline). that'll avoid false positives on low latency models.
[04:30] Nora Patel: and define a manual override, e.g., SecOps can force stop even if thresholds not yet hit.
[04:36] Alicia Chen: agreed, manual kill switch will be in the runbook and as a button in the canary dashboard.

--- Telemetry and dashboards
[04:50] Alicia Chen: Marcus will deliver the canary dashboard link with the three signal groups: latency tails, errors, and quality/regression (prompt set diff). we'll also include token-level cost burn and per-route counts.
[05:06] Marcus Ortiz: quick caveat — the quality/regression signal depends on your eval harness running continuous checks; we'll show sample diffs but you must run your golden prompt set.
[05:20] Liam Howard: we have that, but it needs to be run against live canary traffic snapshots, is there an easy way to schedule that?
[05:28] Marcus Ortiz: yes we can integrate with your CI to pull a sample of canary responses every 10 minutes and run evals, results will feed to the dashboard. small note: transcription sometimes shows model names as 're wood' in our logs, so ignore that artifact — ha.

--- Runbook and rollback playbook specifics
[05:48] Alicia Chen: let's review steps in the runbook: pre-shift checks, canary start, metric windows, auto rollback conditions, manual escalation, rollback verification, post-mortem. any missing?
[06:02] Sara Martins: add a pre-shift KV warm-up step and a cache priming job; otherwise first few minutes blow the tail.
[06:10] Marcus Ortiz: agree, add 'kv-cache priming' as step 1b, with a scripted job that hits a representative prefix set.
[06:18] Liam Howard: also include a blue-green compatibility route for model variant fallback — e.g., if quantized path fails, fall back to full-fp32 instance with higher cost.
[06:29] Marcus Ortiz: we support automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we'll add policy examples in the runbook with cost gates.
[06:38] Tomas Vega: security question — if we fail over to fallback model in a different region, what about data residency?
[06:46] Priya Rao: the policy will be region-aware; Redwood routing respects region pins and won't cross the boundary unless you explicitly allow it. we'll document that.

--- Dry-run scheduling and mechanics
[06:58] Alicia Chen: ok proposed dry-run next Wednesday Nov 25th in staging: simulated ramp to 5% then 25% then back down, with a safety hold and manual abort points. Sara, can you get the traffic generator ready?
[07:12] Sara Martins: yes, i'll have a config and runbook fragment by Monday 23rd. noted.
[07:18] Marcus Ortiz: i'll provide the dashboard link and the automation script to shift weights via the API; we can run a rehearsed 'abort' to test rollback logic.
[07:28] Nora Patel: we'll join on-call for the dry-run to observe and to test notification hooks.

--- Security and compliance thread
[07:40] Tomas Vega: for KMS we need: key rotation cadence, ability to audit envelope keys, HSM attestation. also want to see the audit logs format to verify event types.
[07:54] Priya Rao: we have a security pack pdf, but Tomas we'll send the detailed logs schema and KMS integration doc. note: some field names in the logs are truncated, transcription often shows 'KV cash' — that's just the speech-to-text.
[08:06] Alicia Chen: we'll add a separate security call if needed; Tomas, what's your timeline to review?
[08:12] Tomas Vega: target EOD next Tuesday, 2026-11-25 to respond with questions.

--- Questions from GreenWave
[08:24] Liam Howard: if the canary fails and we auto-rollback, how do we ensure no partial writes or side effects? we have stateful downstreams.
[08:33] Marcus Ortiz: recommended pattern is idempotent outputs and write-behind gating: responses underneath a canary tag until commit window. we can also do double-write with eventual reconcile. we'll include patterns in the runbook.
[08:46] Sara Martins: are there examples of customers using session-affinity-aware ramps?
[08:50] Alicia Chen: yes, we'll share a short case study we ran with a fintech customer — note: redwood-dedicated had a sticky session path that worked well.

--- Live troubleshooting snippets (realistic noise and mis-transcriptions)
[09:05] Marcus Ortiz: (screen share) here's the dashboard prototype — you can see p99 spikes on the left, token burn in the middle, and an eval diff table on the right. the diff is noisy but it surfaces the worst regressions.
[09:26] Nora Patel: i'm seeing a gap in the logs where request IDs don't line up with trace IDs, is that expected?
[09:31] Marcus Ortiz: not expected — that sounds like a log aggregation mapping issue, we'll investigate, possible agent pipeline timestamp skew.
[09:40] Liam Howard: i'm going to mark that as a blocker for the dry-run unless it's benign.
[09:45] Alicia Chen: ok we put that as an action item for Marcus and Sara to validate mapping by Monday.

--- Wrap up, decisions and recap
[09:58] Alicia Chen: recap: dry-run staging on 2026-11-25; Marcus to deliver dashboard and automation scripts by 2026-11-22; Marcus to run benches by 2026-11-24; Sara to prep traffic generator by 2026-11-23; Tomas to review KMS/docs and revert by 2026-11-25. auto-rollback policy defined as p99 > baseline + max(250ms,25%) for two windows or error rate > 1%. manual abort will be available.
[10:28] Liam Howard: sounds good, thanks.
[10:34] Tomas Vega: i'll follow up with specific security asks in email.
[10:38] Priya Rao: i'll upload the security pack and the runbook draft after the call.
[10:44] Alicia Chen: perfect. next sync early the week after the dry-run to review results — i'll send calendar invite. thanks everyone.

[11:00] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of "KV cache", 'redwood dedics' for Redwood Dedicated). Action items and next steps captured in metadata above.
